account.$comment: Profile for auth: fresh — the harness registers this account through the app's own sign-up API (lib/account.mjs). nickname defaults to name, birthYear to this year − age.

persona.purpose: Find a paid internship or job lead near Berkeley for after graduation; skeptical of new apps.

language.notes: Native English; not used to app conventions like swipe cards or icon-only buttons.

persona.backstory: I mostly use my phone for texting, email and Handshake when the career center tells me to. My little sister said this app has internships. I'm not giving my info to some random app unless it's clearly legit. Icons without words lose me.
quitsWhen: It wants my info before I know what it is
I can't find the internship part
It looks like a dating or party app
persona.voice: Plain, slightly skeptical, polite. 'I don't get what this button does', 'Is this legit?'

scenario.title: Find an internship near Berkeley
scenario.goal: You need a paid internship (summer or part-time) somewhere near Berkeley / the Bay Area. Use the app to find one that looks real and open, and open its details so you know how to apply.

success.description: An internship listing's detail page is open (reached by the persona — the run starts on /).

environment.summary: Local stack: this worktree's server + built web app, fresh seeded FileStore per run, no secrets, no worker.
knownLimits: Dining menus and RSF gym crowd levels need live campus sources (the local stack runs with CAMPUS_LIVE=0) — empty or missing data there is not a UX bug.
AI features (Ask Lumi, AI profile draft on /start, conversation starters) need an OpenAI key; none is configured locally.
Course catalog is the real Berkeley Class Schedule (6619 courses, Fall 2026 + Spring 2027), fetched 2026-11-05 with the worker's adapter. Seat counts and very recent changes may differ from live.

Campus events, free food, internships, hackathons and scholarships are a read-only snapshot of live (1272 real items, 106 events this week, taken 2026-11-08 19:15 UTC) plus the CSV calendar. Nothing new appears during the run; Q&A and reviews are empty.
No e-mail is sent: the sign-up / sign-in code is shown on screen in the hint (live sends a real e-mail).
Real-time updates (SSE) work locally; other people never reply unless the stack was started with --autoreply.

Signed in as a brand-new real (non-sample, e-mail-verified) account made for this run. Other students exist only if the scenario seeds peers (local fixtures); sample profiles are hidden from real accounts, as on live.
